axioms.relation: R is a subset of M x M.
axioms.reflexive: For every x in M: xRx.
axioms.symmetric: For every x,y in M: xRy implies yRx.
axioms.transitive: For every x,y,z in M: (xRy and yRz) implies xRz.
axioms.equivalence: All three properties on the same specified domain.
axioms.counterexample_logic: One instance refutes a universal property; failure does not mean every instance fails.

domains.lines: All Euclidean straight lines in one fixed plane, considered as infinite geometric sets.
domains.order: All real numbers with ordinary < and <=.
domains.figures: Euclidean geometric figures with congruence defined by existence of an isometry.
domains.segments: All ordinary nondegenerate plane segments as unordered endpoint sets; allowing degenerate segments leaves full-domain verdicts unchanged.
domains.polygons: Bounded plane polygons having well-defined ordinary area.
domains.central_symmetry_center: One fixed O, the same for every related pair.

equality_inclusive.definition: a P b iff dir(a)=dir(b), with unoriented line directions; coincidence is included.
equality_inclusive.plane_set_equivalent_definition: a=b OR a intersection b is empty.
equality_inclusive.basis: Equality of directions; required mathematically by table +,+,+ and supplied parallel-class prose.

strict_disjoint.definition: a Q b iff they are coplanar and a intersection b is empty.
strict_disjoint.counterexample: a:y=0, b:y=1, c=a. aQb and bQc but not aQc.
strict_disjoint.restricted_domain_note: If the domain has no strict-parallel pairs, transitivity is vacuous, but reflexivity still fails for a nonempty domain.

table_derivations.derivation: Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from equality of directions.
No line is perpendicular to itself; right-angle incidence is symmetric. a:y=0, b:x=0, c:y=1 gives a perpendicular b and b perpendicular c, but not a perpendicular c.
Identity isometry, inverse isometry and composition prove the respective properties.
x<x is false; 0<1 but not 1<0; x<y and y<z imply x<z.
x<=x; 0<=1 but not 1<=0; x<=y and y<=z imply x<=z.

no_properties.derivation: Diagonals are absent, reverse (2,1) is absent, and (1,3) required by the displayed chain is absent.

partition_derivation.definition: Nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks covering M.
partition_to_equivalence: Coverage gives every x a block, proving xRx.
Blocks for x,y and y,z share y and thus are identical, proving xRz.
equivalence_to_partition: Define [x]={y in M:xRy}; reflexivity makes it nonempty and provides coverage.
If t in [x] intersection [z], xRt and zRt; symmetry and transitivity give xRz.
For u in [x], zRx and xRu imply zRu. Reverse the argument to get [x]=[z].
xRy implies equal classes; if [x]=[y], y in [y]=[x] implies xRy.
partition_derivation.parallel_application: Every class contains all lines with one direction, including each member itself; fig-213 illustrates only samples.

exercises.derivation: Length equals itself; equality reverses; equality of length(s),length(t) and length(t),length(u) gives length(s)=length(u).
exercises.classes: All segments of each fixed length, independent of position or orientation.

parts.derivation: The three properties are those of equality of the area value.
parts.distinction_example: Rectangles with side lengths 1,4 and 2,2 both have area 4 but are not congruent.

parts.relation: Images of segments under central symmetry about one fixed O.
parts.definition: xRy iff y=H(x), with H(p)=2O-p and H([A,B])=[H(A),H(B)].

derivations.fixed_instances: A nondegenerate segment is fixed exactly when its midpoint is O; this does not make the full-domain relation reflexive.
derivations.transitivity_failure: Let y=H(x) for that non-fixed x and z=x. Then xRy and yRz, but xRz is false. Two images yield z=x, not z=H(x).

parts.restricted_fixed_domain: On only H-fixed segments the relation is identity and is an equivalence; this is a different domain.
parts.orbit_relation_is_different: y=x OR y=H(x) is an equivalence with orbits of size one or two. Do not substitute it for the given relation.

readings.definition: There exists p with p in a and p in b.
readings.derivation: Each line shares its points with itself. Intersection nonemptiness is symmetric. a:y=0, b:x=0, c:y=1 provides two intersecting pairs but a,c are disjoint.

readings.definition: There exists common p such that every common q equals p.
readings.derivation: A line shares infinitely many points with itself. Unique intersection is symmetric. The same three distinct lines give two unique intersections but no intersection of a,c.

parts.stable_conclusion: Not an equivalence relation under either reading.

examples.proof: Equality of lengths is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
Equality of areas is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

examples.domain: All lines of a fixed plane
